From playtest 0001 (`docs/playtest/0001-commander-seat.md`, response in `docs/playtest/0001-response.md`). Three separate defects on the same surface, batched because they are all `cti_fnc_mapRender` and all presentation — none of them needs the Observation to change.

Every visual choice in that function is a playtest-tuned placeholder in ADR-0020's sense, and this is the playtest that was supposed to judge them. The verdict was that they cost more than they should.

## 1. Nothing on the map says which Place is selected

Verbatim:

> Some visual feedback on what location I've selected whilst issuing orders would improve usability

Today the only feedback is the hint's `Place:` line. `cti_fnc_mapCommander`'s `MapSingleClick` handler sets `cti_uiPlace` and re-renders, and `cti_fnc_mapRender` draws nothing for it. The Commander is clicking on the map and reading the answer somewhere else.

Acceptance criterion, automatable in an in-world probe: after a `MapSingleClick` that resolves to a Place, a local marker distinct from the Squad and Contact markers exists at that Place's position; a click on open country removes it, because `cti_fnc_placeOf` deliberately selects nothing there.

## 2. Marker text collides with the engine's own town labels

Verbatim:

> I see squad 1's marker right on top of the Agia Marina marker and a warning that 'team foot - seen 72s ago' on top of that. None are legible because of the collission in label text location.

Evidence: `docs/playtest/0001-marker-collision-zoomed-out.png` and `-zoomed-in.png`.

This is structural, not bad luck. `setMarkerTextLocal` renders text at the marker position; a Place's position is the town centre; the town centre is exactly where Arma prints its own town name. So a Squad marker, a Contact marker and the engine's label collide at every Place, every time. The zoomed-in screenshot also shows red-on-terrain is weak at that scale even where nothing overlaps.

Acceptance criteria: Squad and Contact markers at the same Place do not draw their text at the same point, and neither draws over the engine's label position. `setMarkerPosLocal` with a per-kind offset is the cheap answer; anything that separates them is acceptable.

## 3. Squad strength has no denominator

Verbatim:

> As commander I should be able to see a marker per squad showing their location and strength (e.g. 4/8).

`cti_fnc_mapRender` writes `format [\"%1 %2/%3 — %4 %5\", id, type, size, order, place]`, which renders `WEST-1 rifle/8`. The `8` is live current strength — `SquadView.size` is what the daemon currently counts — so the slash reads as a fraction and is not one. A Squad down to four men renders `rifle/4`, and nothing on screen says four of what.

Acceptance criterion: the marker text carries current strength against establishment strength, and the establishment figure comes from the same catalogue the price does rather than being written down again in SQF (see #159 for the precedent — `fn_effectApply` inventing an 8-man size for a fact the daemon owns).

## Not in scope here

The fourth marker defect from the same session — a Squad in open ground having no marker at all — needs the Observation wire to change and is filed separately.
